title: Count the Votes That Remain
description: A five-node coordination cluster loses two nodes. The remaining three can communicate. What can a majority-based consensus protocol still do?

options.text: Commit decisions with the remaining majority.
options.explanation: A five-node group needs floor(5/2)+1 = 3 votes, so it tolerates two failures while those three can communicate.

options.text: Only serve writes after all five return.
options.explanation: Unanimity is not required. Waiting for all nodes would discard the protocol's failure tolerance.

options.text: Let each surviving node elect itself independently.
options.explanation: Independent ownership would defeat agreement. Elections and commits must satisfy the protocol's quorum rules.

options.text: Add one node to tolerate three failures in a six-node group.
options.explanation: Six nodes need four votes and still tolerate only two failures. Seven nodes are needed to tolerate three.
